text:
The son will most likely **prevail**, because the written contract made him an intended third-party beneficiary by directing the $5,000 to him. The landscaper's later request to be paid instead was an unsupported change to the owner's duty, so the owner's payment to the father did not discharge the obligation owed to the son. This revises my earlier answer, which treated the son's unvested rights as letting the father and owner modify the contract.

CONFIDENCE: 80
